description: As humanity prepares for future exploration of Mars, understanding where and how astronauts can safely travel will be essential. Our project brings together NASA data from multiple missions into an interactive Martian map, allowing users to explore routes, examine terrain and environmental conditions, identify potential hazards, and discover scientifically interesting locations. Safer Marswalks. Greater discoveries.
summary:
Orbit & Origin is a full-stack Mars exploration and mission-planning platform developed to make NASA’s scientific data more accessible, interactive, and useful for understanding the Martian environment.

Developed for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, our project integrates satellite imagery, terrain analysis, potential hazards, scientific points of interest, and route-planning capabilities into a unified platform.

Our prototype focuses on the Jezero Crater region, allowing us to prioritize detailed scientific analysis within a defined area of Mars. By combining NASA Mars Trek imagery, MOLA elevation data, and HiRISE digital terrain models, users can explore the Martian surface, examine elevation and slope measurements, and identify potential exploration risks.

The platform also incorporates the A* (A-star) pathfinding algorithm to support route planning based on available terrain information.

Built using React, React Leaflet, Python, FastAPI, NumPy, and Rasterio, Orbit & Origin connects interactive mapping with scientific data processing.

Our goal is to demonstrate how NASA’s open data can support informed exploration decisions, encourage scientific discovery, and make planetary science more accessible through an engaging educational experience.
details:
Orbit & Origin is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge.

The project aims to make complex Martian scientific data more accessible by integrating satellite imagery, terrain measurements, potential hazards, scientific points of interest, and route-planning capabilities into one interactive platform.

Rather than attempting to provide detailed terrain analysis across the entire planet, our team focused on the Jezero Crater region of Mars. This approach allowed us to concentrate on a defined exploration area, integrate relevant scientific datasets, and develop a more focused solution for analyzing terrain conditions and planning potential exploration routes.

Our platform is built around three core functions: Explore, Analyze, and Plan.

How Our Platform Works

Explore—Interactive Mars Mapping

Users can navigate an interactive map of the Martian surface, zoom into different locations, select geographic coordinates, and view markers representing potential hazards and scientific points of interest.

The map brings geographic and scientific information together in one interface, helping users understand the environment and identify locations relevant to exploration.

Analyze—Terrain and Scientific Data

Orbit & Origin integrates NASA elevation datasets to provide terrain information for supported locations.

When a user selects a location, the frontend sends its coordinates to the backend through a REST API. The backend accesses the available scientific datasets and returns terrain measurements, including elevation and slope.

These measurements help users evaluate the physical characteristics of the Martian surface and understand how terrain conditions may influence exploration decisions.

Our platform incorporates the A* (A-star) pathfinding algorithm* to support route generation between selected starting points and destinations.

A* is a pathfinding algorithm that searches for a route by evaluating possible movements toward a destination. Its use provides a foundation for algorithm-based exploration planning.

The route-planning interface brings generated paths together with available terrain and hazard information, allowing users to examine potential exploration routes within the capabilities and geographic coverage of the prototype.

NASA Data Integration

A key aspect of Orbit & Origin is its integration of scientific resources from NASA missions.

NASA Mars Trek — Surface Imagery

We use imagery accessed through NASA Mars Trek to provide the visual representation of the Martian surface. This allows users to interact with geographic locations and examine surface features within the mapping interface.

MOLA — Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter

MOLA, an instrument aboard NASA's Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft, collected measurements used to develop topographic maps of Mars.

Our project uses MOLA elevation data stored in IMG raster format. This dataset supports broader terrain elevation analysis within the region covered by the selected data product.

HiRISE — High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment

HiRISE, an instrument aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, provides high-resolution observations of the Martian surface.

We integrated a HiRISE-derived Digital Terrain Model (DTM) stored in GeoTIFF format to support more detailed local elevation and slope analysis.

Why We Combined MOLA and HiRISE

MOLA and HiRISE provide complementary information at different spatial resolutions. MOLA supports broader topographic analysis, while the HiRISE terrain model provides more detailed measurements within its geographic coverage.

By combining these datasets, Orbit & Origin demonstrates how different NASA scientific resources can contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of a selected Martian location.

Technical Implementation

Orbit & Origin was developed as a full-stack web application using modern web-development technologies and geospatial data-processing tools.

Frontend Development

We used React to develop the user interface, with Leaflet and React Leaflet supporting interactive mapping, geographic markers, and map navigation. Three.js was also included in our 3D development work.

Backend Development

The backend was developed using Python and FastAPI, providing REST API endpoints that connect the frontend to the scientific data-processing components.

We used NumPy for numerical operations and Rasterio for accessing and processing geospatial raster datasets, including the MOLA IMG data and HiRISE GeoTIFF terrain model.

When users request terrain information, the backend processes the relevant coordinates and returns the available measurements in JSON format for display in the frontend.

Development and Collaboration Tools

We used Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration, Visual Studio Code for software development, and Swagger UI for inspecting and testing backend API endpoints.

Innovation and Design Considerations

Orbit & Origin combines scientific data integration, interactive mapping, and algorithm-based route planning within a single exploration environment.

Rather than presenting Mars as a static image, the platform allows users to interact with available scientific measurements and explore how terrain information can contribute to mission-planning decisions.

Our team deliberately focused on the Jezero Crater region to prioritize meaningful data integration over attempting incomplete planet-wide analysis.

Several technical factors influenced our approach, including geographic coordinate handling, terrain elevation and slope, differences in dataset resolution, geographic coverage, and the challenges of processing large scientific raster files.

We also considered how scientific information could be presented through an interface that is understandable to users without extensive experience in planetary science.

Because detailed HiRISE terrain coverage is limited, not every location within the wider map can provide the same level of analysis. Orbit & Origin is therefore presented as a research and educational prototype rather than a validated astronaut-navigation or mission-safety system.

Orbit & Origin demonstrates how NASA's open scientific data can be combined with software engineering and geospatial technologies to create accessible tools for planetary exploration.

Intended Impact and Future Development

Orbit & Origin demonstrates how NASA's scientific datasets can be integrated with modern software technologies to support a more accessible and interactive approach to Mars exploration.

By combining real terrain measurements, hazard information, and A* route planning, our platform helps users examine the Martian environment and understand how geographic conditions can influence exploration decisions.

Beyond its technical applications, Orbit & Origin has potential educational value. The platform could introduce students and aspiring engineers to planetary science, geospatial data analysis, and algorithm-based problem-solving through an interactive experience.

Our current prototype focuses on the Jezero Crater region, where we prioritized detailed terrain analysis using available MOLA and HiRISE datasets. Future development could expand coverage to additional Martian regions, integrate further scientific datasets, and improve route evaluation and mission-planning capabilities.

Ultimately, our goal is to develop Orbit & Origin into a more comprehensive platform that connects scientific observations with practical exploration tools, making planetary data easier to understand, analyze, and apply.
